title: Albion, through the years — Marie’s interactive club museum
description: Explore Marie’s interactive Albion museum: eras, players, match stories, historical photographs and unusual objects from West Bromwich Albion’s past.

blocks.field4: From the spring works to Wembley. From the first cup to the Great Escape. Explore the people, places and little things behind a lifetime of Albion.
blocks.field6: Take your time. There’s history here.
blocks.field10: The boys of 1888. A cup-winning beginning.
blocks.field11: ADMIT ONE · A LIFETIME OF FOOTBALL

blocks.field2: A Grand National winner visited The Hawthorns.
blocks.field3: Red Rum was a special guest at John Osborne’s testimonial in May 1978. A memorable night, even before the football began.
blocks.field4: Let Baggie Bird show you the story →
blocks.field5: Albion’s title once fitted in a pocket.
blocks.field6: A matchbox cover celebrated the 1920 championship with stripes and a team photograph. A tiny object with a big story.
blocks.field8: Not every goalkeeper wore a different shirt.
blocks.field9: Joe Reader’s surviving kit is believed to date from 1900/01. Like his teammates, he wore stripes — with long trousers.
blocks.field11: The song thrush has a familiar local name.
blocks.field12: A throstle is a song thrush. Hawthorn trees, its favoured habitat, inspired the ground’s name and feature with the bird in Albion’s crest.
blocks.field16: Baggie Bird, illustrated in Albion’s navy and white stripes, raising a welcoming wing

blocks.field3: Open a story behind the silverware.
blocks.field8: In 1968, Jeff Astle scored the only goal against Everton in extra time. It completed a cup run in which he scored in every round.
blocks.field14: Albion finished the first league season after the First World War as champions, scoring 104 goals and collecting 60 points under the two-points-for-a-win system.
blocks.field20: Before the League Cup final moved to Wembley, Albion overcame West Ham 5–3 on aggregate to lift the trophy in 1966.
blocks.field22: Also in the cabinet: the Charity Shield in 1920 and 1954 (shared), alongside further league and youth honours.

blocks.field3: Albion’s home since 1900. A place for matchday rituals, familiar faces and the next generation’s first game.
